name: Clifton Brown

summary.text: Clifton Brown is a carpenter running as an unaffiliated candidate for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District.
He earned a high school diploma from Cherry Creek High School in 1976.
His campaign platform centers on ending gerrymandering by eliminating congressional districts, campaign finance reform, and housing affordability.

research_notes: Brown's Ballotpedia survey and campaign site (ruhero.com) describe a platform of ending gerrymandering by abolishing congressional districts entirely, banning PAC/corporate money and outside income for officeholders, capping interest rates at 12%, a 32-hour workweek, and cutting military spending/closing foreign bases. None of these map cleanly onto the 25 statements without stretching (his redistricting position is about eliminating districts outright, not about Colorado's independent commission versus mid-decade redraws, so it was not coded against the redistricting-commission statement). No position found on abortion, guns, immigration enforcement, taxes, or any Colorado ballot measure specifically. Build review 2026-10-14: removed inferred position(s) on public-lands; the source states a general principle and does not name that policy area.
